## IRouteReply type

Route atom: forced single-message send.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type IRouteReply = INeverFields<`editOptions` | `fallbackOptions` | `fallback`> & {
    mode: `reply`;
    keyboard?: IInBoKb | null;
    rich?: IOptReplyRich[0] | null;
    richOptions?: IOptRichSend | null;
    options?: IOptReply | null;
    broadcast?: null | undefined;
    chunkSize?: null | undefined;
};
```
**References:** [INeverFields](./gramstax.ineverfields.md)<!-- -->, [IInBoKb](./gramstax.iinbokb.md)<!-- -->, [IOptReplyRich](./gramstax.ioptreplyrich.md)<!-- -->, [IOptRichSend](./gramstax.ioptrichsend.md)<!-- -->, [IOptReply](./gramstax.ioptreply.md)

## Remarks

`mode: 'reply'` always sends a new message, even from a callback query, so no edit can happen: the edit-only keys (`editOptions`<!-- -->, `fallbackOptions`<!-- -->) and `fallback` are never read — a forced reply never edits, so there is no edit to fall back from. `richOptions` stays live here because the rich SEND still happens; only the rich EDIT is unreachable.
